Control: Product security governance and secure development lifecycle
Summary: A product security policy with a named accountable executive, and one secure development lifecycle applied to every product line from design to end of support.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Product security policy and SDL standard with RACI; per-release SDL gate record generated by the pipeline (see E1).
Build to: CRA: the lifecycle must deliver risk-appropriate security across design, development and production.
EU CRA note: Design, develop and produce to an appropriate level of cybersecurity based on the risks; Part II presupposes an operating lifecycle.
UK PSTI note: Three outcome requirements only; no lifecycle duty.
US CTM clauses: FCC 24-26 para 27 (declaration that the applicant 'has taken every reasonable measure to create a securable product')
US CTM note: Implies a process; no SDL requirement in the rules read.
JC-STAR note: STAR-1 tests product outcomes only.
SG CLS clauses: CCC SP-151-2 5.2.1, 5.2.3 (Level 3 lifecycle provisions CK-LP-01 to CK-LP-08)

Summary: A documented risk assessment per product family that states, item by item, which security properties apply and why any do not, updated through the support period.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Risk assessment per product family with Annex I applicability table and residual-risk register (Annex VII point 3).
Build to: CRA: documented, product-level, with a justification for each non-applied requirement.
EU CRA note: Justify every Annex I Part I (2) item not applied; one assessment per family allowed (guidance paras 174-177).
US CTM note: The baseline is risk-derived by NIST; manufacturers are not asked for their own assessment in the rules read.
JC-STAR clauses: JST-SR-03-01-2026 (STAR-3 N/A conditions justified with evidence)
JC-STAR note: STAR-3 only.
SG CLS clauses: CCC SP-151-2 5.2.1 (IMDA IoT Cyber Security Guide)

Control: Regime scope and product classification register
Summary: One register listing every product, its markets, the regimes that apply, any exception relied on, its CRA class and its conformity route.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Portfolio applicability register with legal basis per row, reviewed quarterly (feeds E3 classification).
Build to: CRA: classification decides whether a notified body is needed; PSTI and AU exceptions decide whether a statement is needed.
EU CRA note: Class drives the route: Class I needs a notified body unless a harmonised standard, common specification or substantial-level EU certification scheme is applied in full (Art 32(2)); none exists yet.
UK PSTI clauses: Act ss.4-6; SI 2023/1007 reg 6, Sch 3 (as amended by SI 2025/211)
UK PSTI note: Excepts desktops, laptops, non-cellular tablets, EV charge points, medical devices, smart meters, certain vehicles, NI products under Windsor Framework law.
US CTM note: Voluntary; excludes medical devices, motor vehicles, wired-only, enterprise and industrial products, Covered List equipment.
JC-STAR clauses: IPA JC-STAR (IoT products communicating over IP)
JC-STAR note: Voluntary; STAR-2 to STAR-4 exist only for some product types.
AU SDS clauses: Cyber Security Act 2024 ss 13-14; Rules s 8
AU SDS note: Excepts desktops, laptops, tablets, smartphones, therapeutic goods, road vehicles.

Summary: An intake gate for every third-party and open-source component, with security review, known-vulnerability check and recorded decision.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Component intake records per component and version, linked to the SBOM.
Build to: CRA: covers every component, including free open-source software.
EU CRA note: Due diligence on all integrated components, including non-commercial FOSS.
US CTM clauses: FCC 24-26 (product includes companion apps and cloud)
US CTM note: The applicant answers for the whole product; no component process prescribed.
JC-STAR note: STAR-3 only.
SG CLS clauses: CCC SP-151-2 5.2.4, 5.4 (binary analysis covers third-party components)

Summary: Screen the applicant, its affiliates and the product's components against the FCC Covered List, Commerce Entity List, DoD Chinese Military Companies list and federal debarment lists before a US label application, and again on change.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Signed screening record per product and supplier, kept with the label application.
Build to: US CTM only.
EU CRA note: No origin-based eligibility test in the CRA.
US CTM clauses: FCC 24-26 para 27 (declarations 2-5, under penalty of perjury); 47 CFR 1.50002
US CTM note: Unique to the US programme; failure to cure within 20 days can end the authorisation (para 28).
JC-STAR note: Not required.

Summary: Ship in a secure default state (optional services off, debug locked, onboarding enforced) and let the user reset to that state.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Default-configuration export per release; onboarding and reset test results.
Build to: CRA: whole default state plus reset.
EU CRA note: Secure by default with reset to the original state; tailor-made carve-out only.
UK PSTI note: Covers only the password part of the default state.
US CTM clauses: NIST IR 8425 s.2.2.1 Product Configuration; registry secure-configuration guidance
US CTM note: Registry tells users how to configure the product securely.
JC-STAR note: State persists after outages; secure-setup information; no full default-state rule.

Summary: Every password is unique per device and not derivable from public data or identifiers, or is set by the user at first use.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Credential-provisioning design note; test showing no shared or derivable passwords across a production sample.
Build to: JC-STAR STAR-1 for the length rule; PSTI and AU for the derivation tests. Build to both.
EU CRA note: Implied by secure default and access control; not stated in these words.
UK PSTI note: Unique per product or user-defined; not incremental, public-derived, identifier-derived or guessable.
US CTM clauses: NIST IR 8425 s.2.2.1 Interface Access Control; registry default-password guidance
US CTM note: Registry explains how to change the default password.
JC-STAR note: Unique and at least 6 characters, or forced change on first use to at least 8: the only numeric threshold.

Summary: Only the interfaces needed in each state are enabled; debug ports are locked; development tooling is stripped; network services default to deny.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Interface inventory per product state; external port scan; debug-lock evidence.
Build to: CRA and JC-STAR STAR-1 are equivalent in effect.
EU CRA note: Limit attack surfaces, including external interfaces.
US CTM clauses: NIST IR 8425 s.2.2.1 Interface Access Control
US CTM note: Access control on interfaces; disabling unused ones is not stated as such.
JC-STAR note: Disable unnecessary high-risk TCP/UDP ports, Bluetooth and USB.

Summary: Memory-safe languages or hardened builds (ASLR, W^X, CFI), sandboxing, privilege separation and input validation.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Compiler-flag and binary-hardening scan output per build; fuzzing reports.
Build to: CRA only.
EU CRA note: Reduce incident impact with exploitation mitigation mechanisms.
US CTM note: Not an IR 8425 outcome.
JC-STAR note: STAR-3 only.
SG CLS note: Lab testing at Levels 3-4 would surface weaknesses; no design rule.

Control: No known exploitable vulnerabilities at release
Summary: Release gate that correlates the release SBOM with EUVD, CVE/NVD and the CISA KEV catalogue and blocks release unless each finding is fixed or mitigated.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Release-gate scan report with KEV status and decisions, per version.
Build to: CRA: applies at placing on the market and is judged against public databases.
EU CRA note: 'Known' includes EUVD and other prominent databases (guidance C(2026) 5252 paras 233-234).
US CTM note: Ongoing duty to identify critical vulnerabilities and issue updates; not a release gate.
JC-STAR note: A vulnerability scan must find no known exploitable vulnerabilities.

Control: Authentication and access control on every interface
Summary: Every local, network, app and cloud interface authenticates the caller and enforces roles; privileged roles use MFA; unauthorised access is reported.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Access-control model per interface; negative test results; alert catalogue.
Build to: CRA: adds the duty to report possible unauthorised access.
EU CRA note: Authentication, identity or access management, and reporting of possible unauthorised access.
US CTM clauses: NIST IR 8425 s.2.2.1 Interface Access Control
US CTM note: Restrict logical access to authorised entities.
JC-STAR note: Access to protected information over IP controlled by appropriate authentication.

Summary: Users can change every authentication value; network login resists brute force (rate limiting or lockout); machine credentials expire.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Credential-change and brute-force test results.
Build to: JC-STAR STAR-1: explicit, testable requirements.
EU CRA note: Implied by protection from unauthorised access.
UK PSTI note: User-defined passwords allowed; no change or brute-force rule.
US CTM clauses: NIST IR 8425 s.2.2.1 Interface Access Control
US CTM note: Outcome-level only until the technical requirements are final.
JC-STAR note: Authentication values changeable; brute-force resistance for non-constrained devices.

Summary: Model, hardware and software version visible to the user; type, batch or serial number marked; the manufacturer can identify every logical and physical component.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Marking specification; screenshot of version display; component inventory per version.
Build to: CRA plus IR 8425: physical marking and a component-level inventory.
EU CRA note: Type, batch or serial number or other identifying element on the product.
UK PSTI note: Product type and batch only in the statement of compliance.
US CTM note: Product and components uniquely identifiable.
JC-STAR note: Model number visible on the device, UI or companion app.
SG CLS note: No identification requirement found in the specification read.
AU SDS note: Product type and batch only in the statement of compliance.

Control: Confidentiality of data at rest and in transit
Summary: Encrypt relevant data at rest and in transit with approved algorithms and protected keys; no plaintext fallback.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Cryptographic inventory; TLS and downgrade test results; key-management design.
Build to: CRA: covers stored, transmitted and otherwise processed data.
EU CRA note: Encrypting relevant data at rest or in transit by state-of-the-art mechanisms.
US CTM note: Protect data at rest and in transit.
JC-STAR note: Secure storage including removable media; protection against eavesdropping.

Control: Integrity of software, data and configuration
Summary: Verified boot and signed software, signed configuration, integrity monitoring, and reporting of corruption.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Boot-chain and signature test results; corruption-detection test.
Build to: CRA: also requires reporting of corruption.
EU CRA note: Protect integrity of data, commands, programs and configuration; report on corruptions.
US CTM clauses: NIST IR 8425 s.2.2.1 Data Protection, Software Update
US CTM note: Integrity of updates and data; secure boot not named.
JC-STAR note: STAR-1 checks update integrity; secure boot only at STAR-3.

Summary: Collect and process only the data each function needs; telemetry off by default where not needed; defined retention.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Data inventory for the default configuration; retention schedule.
Build to: CRA only (GDPR applies separately).
EU CRA note: Adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary.
US CTM note: No minimisation outcome among the IR 8425 capabilities.
JC-STAR note: Not in STAR-1.
SG CLS note: Personal-data provisions where Level 2 is claimed.

Summary: Users can permanently remove all data and settings, and transfer data securely where transfer is offered.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Write-erase-read test per data type; export test; user instructions.
Build to: CRA: adds secure transfer; JC-STAR adds the firmware-version check.
EU CRA note: Securely and easily remove on a permanent basis; secure transfer where data can be transferred.
US CTM note: Deletion sub-outcome not re-read for this module; verify against IR 8425 Table 3.
JC-STAR note: Users can delete collected data, settings, authentication values and keys; firmware version unchanged.

Summary: Updates are signed with protected keys, verified before install, protected against rollback, installed atomically with recovery, and persist across power loss.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Update design note; signature, rollback and recovery test results.
Build to: CRA: adds anti-rollback and recovery through the secure-distribution duty.
EU CRA clauses: Annex I Part I (2)(c); Part II (7)
EU CRA note: Security updates and secure distribution mechanisms.
UK PSTI note: PSTI requires the support period to be published, not an update capability.
US CTM note: Software updatable by authorised entities through a secure, configurable mechanism.
JC-STAR note: Updatable, version verifiable, persists after power-off; integrity checked before applying.

Control: Automatic updates by default, with user control
Summary: Security updates install automatically by default where applicable, with notification, postponement and a clear opt-out.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Default-configuration proof; opt-out and notification UI evidence.
Build to: CRA: automatic by default is the rule, not a disclosure.
EU CRA note: Automatic by default where applicable, with an easy opt-out, notification and postponement.
US CTM clauses: Registry: whether updates are automatic (programme launch, 7 Jan 2025)
US CTM note: Disclosure, not a mandate.
JC-STAR note: STAR-1 needs easy, clear update steps; automatic updates only at STAR-3.

Control: Timely, free security updates kept separate from feature updates
Summary: Fix vulnerabilities without delay, free of charge, with advisory text, and separate security from feature updates where technically feasible.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Remediation SLA policy; update release notes with advisory text; pricing terms.
Build to: CRA: free and without delay.
EU CRA note: Without delay; separate where feasible; free of charge with advisory messages.
US CTM note: Promptly issue corrective updates until the support end date.
JC-STAR note: Documented policy for prioritising security updates.

Control: Defined support period: set, published, never shortened
Summary: Set a support period per product from expected use, publish it with an end date, publish any extension promptly, and never shorten it.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Support-period rationale per product; published support-period page with version history.
Build to: CRA sets the length (5-year floor); PSTI and AU set the publication and no-shortening tests.
EU CRA note: At least 5 years unless expected use is shorter; based on reasonable user expectations.
UK PSTI note: Publish; publish extensions as soon as practicable; shortening breaches the requirement.
US CTM note: Support end date in the registry; updates promised until then.
JC-STAR note: Support-end policy in user information; update support while the 2-year label is valid.
SG CLS note: Level 1 treated as equivalent to the PSTI three.
AU SDS note: Expressed as a period with an end date; extensions published; no shortening.

Summary: Keep every security update available for at least 10 years or the rest of the support period, whichever is longer; mark archived versions with risk warnings.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Signed-artefact repository retention policy and index.
Build to: CRA only.
EU CRA note: Each update available for 10 years or the remainder of the support period.
US CTM note: Not required.
JC-STAR note: Not required.

Summary: Machine-readable SBOM per version covering at least top-level dependencies, generated by the build.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): CycloneDX or SPDX SBOM per release in the evidence store (E1).
Build to: CRA.
EU CRA clauses: Annex I Part II (1); Annex VII point 2(b)
EU CRA note: Commonly used machine-readable format; not required to be public.
US CTM note: No SBOM requirement in FCC 24-26 as read; check the final technical requirements.
JC-STAR note: STAR-3 only.
SG CLS note: Lab binary analysis inventories third-party components at Level 3.

Control: Published vulnerability disclosure policy and reporting contact
Summary: Publish a CVD policy with at least one reporting contact, acknowledgement and status-update timelines, in English, free, with no personal data required, plus a human channel.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Public CVD policy page and security.txt; PSIRT procedure; channel test records.
Build to: PSTI wording (timelines, English, no personal data) plus the CRA human channel.
EU CRA note: Enforce a CVD policy; contact address; contact means not limited to automated tools.
UK PSTI note: Contact point; when acknowledgement and status updates will come; accessible, English, free, no personal data.
US CTM clauses: NIST IR 8425 s.2.2.2 Information and Query Reception
US CTM note: Receive and respond to cybersecurity queries.
JC-STAR note: Published policy covering contacts, handling steps and status updates.

Summary: Severity-tiered triage with internal remediation SLAs, a vulnerability register linked to the risk assessment, and status updates to reporters until resolution.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): PSIRT procedure; vulnerability register extract; SLA performance report.
Build to: CRA: remediation duty for all vulnerabilities, not only critical.
EU CRA note: Remediate without delay in relation to the risks; document and update the risk assessment.
UK PSTI note: Status updates promised until resolution; no remediation duty.
US CTM note: Identify critical vulnerabilities and promptly issue updates until the support end date.
JC-STAR note: Handling steps and update-prioritisation policy.

Summary: Threat-driven security testing per release (SAST, fuzzing, scanning) and periodic independent penetration testing, with re-test triggers.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Test plan per product; test and pen-test reports per release (Annex VII point 6).
Build to: CRA for regularity; CTM, JC-STAR STAR-3 and CLS Level 4 for independent testing.
EU CRA note: Effective and regular tests and reviews.
US CTM note: One-off third-party test per label; test procedures not yet final (Oct 2026).
JC-STAR note: STAR-1 vulnerability scan; STAR-3 third-party penetration test.
SG CLS clauses: CCC SP-151-2 5.4 (Level 3 binary analysis); 6.3 (Level 4 penetration test)

Summary: Once a fix is available, publish an advisory (description, affected products, impact, severity, remedy) in human-readable form and CSAF, with any delay justified.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Advisory index; CSAF files; delay decision records.
Build to: CRA.
EU CRA note: Public disclosure of fixed vulnerabilities; delay only in duly justified cases.
US CTM note: Broadcast cybersecurity information to customers.
JC-STAR note: Update notices in user information.

Summary: Report vulnerabilities found in third-party components to their maintainers and share fixes, with a licence check.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Upstream report log; patch-sharing records.
Build to: CRA only.
EU CRA note: Report to the maintainer; share fixes where appropriate in machine-readable form.
US CTM note: Not required.
JC-STAR note: Not required.

Summary: Record security-relevant events (access, configuration and firmware changes) with accurate time, tamper evidence, export, and a user opt-out.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Event catalogue; sample logs; opt-out evidence.
Build to: CRA: logging plus a user opt-out.
EU CRA note: Record and monitor relevant internal activity, with an opt-out for the user.
US CTM clauses: NIST IR 8425 s.2.2.1 Cybersecurity State Awareness
US CTM note: Support detection of incidents; no opt-out rule.
JC-STAR note: STAR-3 only.
SG CLS note: Telemetry examination where Level 2 is claimed.

Control: Availability and resilience of essential functions
Summary: Essential functions survive denial-of-service, network loss and power loss; the product recovers without reverting to an insecure state.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Essential-function list with mitigations; stress, outage and recovery test results.
Build to: CRA.
EU CRA note: Availability of essential and basic functions, also after an incident, including DoS resilience.
US CTM note: No resilience capability.
JC-STAR note: Keep authentication values and updated software after power or network loss.

Control: Limit impact on other devices and networks
Summary: No amplification, egress control, back-off on retries, no open relays; documented emitters.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Emitter inventory; external scans; amplification calculations.
Build to: CRA only.
EU CRA note: Minimise negative impact on other devices or networks.
US CTM note: Not an IR 8425 capability.
JC-STAR note: Not in STAR-1.

Control: Report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents
Summary: A 24-hour capable case process that files early warnings, notifications and final reports on the ENISA Single Reporting Platform to the coordinator CSIRT.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Case records with UTC awareness time and SRP submission receipts (E2 case engine).
Build to: CRA only.
EU CRA note: 24 h / 72 h / final report 14 days after a fix is available for exploited vulnerabilities; 24 h / 72 h / 1 month after the incident notification for severe incidents; live since 11 Sep 2026.
UK PSTI note: No authority reporting of vulnerabilities or incidents.
US CTM note: No authority reporting.
JC-STAR note: No authority reporting.
AU SDS note: No product-vulnerability reporting under Part 2 (Part 3 ransomware reporting is separate and out of scope).

Control: Inform users of exploited vulnerabilities and incidents
Summary: Tell affected users, in a structured machine-readable format where appropriate, about the vulnerability or incident and the mitigations they can take.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): User notification templates; delivery logs.
Build to: CRA.
EU CRA note: Inform impacted users and, where appropriate, all users, in a timely manner; no fixed deadline, and the coordinator CSIRT may inform users if the manufacturer does not.
US CTM note: Broadcast cybersecurity information to customers.
JC-STAR note: Update notices only.

Summary: Plain-language information on secure setup, use, updates, end of support and safe disposal or data erasure, versioned and kept online.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Versioned user security guide and Annex II information per product.
Build to: CRA Annex II content; JC-STAR adds disposal guidance explicitly.
EU CRA note: Annex II information kept available for 10 years or the support period.
UK PSTI note: Reporting and support information must be accessible, clear and transparent.
US CTM clauses: NIST IR 8425 s.2.2.2 Documentation, Product Education and Awareness; registry
US CTM note: Registry carries secure-configuration guidance.
JC-STAR note: Safe setup and use, update notices, support-end policy, disposal and data erasure.

Control: Support end date at the point of sale
Summary: Show the support end date (at least month and year) where the product is offered, alongside the price on the manufacturer's own website.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Point-of-sale template and screenshots per channel.
Build to: CRA for content (month and year); PSTI for placement (beside the price).
EU CRA note: End date including at least month and year, at the time of purchase.
UK PSTI note: Alongside or as prominent as price information on own or non-paid websites.
US CTM clauses: Registry support period via the label QR code
US CTM note: Reachable from the label, not required on the listing.
JC-STAR clauses: IPA product list (label status and expiry)
JC-STAR note: Label status, not the support end date.
AU SDS note: Prominent alongside the product's main characteristics on manufacturer-controlled websites.

Control: Security label and public registry listing
Summary: Apply for and maintain voluntary security labels where the market values them, keep the registry entry accurate, and control label artwork and QR codes.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Label register per SKU and market: label ID, level, expiry, registry URL.
Build to: US CTM: label plus QR registry with prescribed data.
EU CRA note: CE marking signals conformity but is not a security label.
UK PSTI note: No label; a valid JC-STAR STAR-1 or CLS label gives deemed compliance under SI 2025/1267.
US CTM clauses: FCC 24-26 paras 55, 78 (FCC IoT Label: Cyber Trust Mark plus QR code to registry)
US CTM note: Only CLA-authorised products may carry the label.
JC-STAR clauses: IPA press release 25 Mar 2025 (label with QR code to product page)
JC-STAR note: STAR level shown; 2-year validity.
SG CLS note: Label awarded by CCC at the level achieved.

Control: Manufacturer identification and single point of contact
Summary: Manufacturer name, trade mark, postal and electronic contact on the product, packaging or documents, and a single point of contact for vulnerability reporting.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Marking specification; contact page.
Build to: CRA.
EU CRA note: Identification and contact details; single point of contact not limited to automated tools.
UK PSTI note: Name and address in the statement of compliance.
US CTM note: Applicant identified to the CLA; registry content not fully read.
JC-STAR note: Security contact shown on the IPA page.
AU SDS note: Names and addresses, including authorised representatives in Australia, in the statement.

Summary: One evidence store per product version holding design, risk, test, SBOM and vulnerability-handling evidence, from which each regime's file is assembled.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Annex VII technical file generated per version by the pipeline (E1).
Build to: CRA.
EU CRA note: Drawn up before placing on the market and kept up to date.
UK PSTI note: Records of investigations of compliance failures only.
US CTM clauses: FCC 24-26 (application with lab test report to the CLA)
US CTM note: Test report and application file, not a full technical file.
JC-STAR clauses: JST-CR-01-01-2024 (STAR-1 conformance checklist and evaluation methods)
JC-STAR note: Checklist with evidence per requirement.
SG CLS note: Evidence reviewed by the test lab and CCC.
AU SDS note: Examination powers imply evidence on request.

Control: Declaration of conformity or statement of compliance
Summary: Issue each regime's declaration from the same evidence: EU declaration, UK statement of compliance, US label declaration, JC-STAR self-declaration, CLS declaration, Australian statement.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Declaration generator with per-regime templates; signed declarations per product and batch.
Build to: All regimes require one; formats differ. The CRA declaration is the most demanding (languages, CE marking).
EU CRA note: In the languages of sale; one single declaration covering every Union act that requires one (Art 28(3)); simplified version gives the full declaration's URL.
UK PSTI note: Must accompany the product; seven content items including the defined support period and standards relied on.
US CTM note: Declaration under penalty of perjury with the application.
JC-STAR note: Checklist-based self-declaration to IPA.
AU SDS clauses: Cyber Security Act 2024 s 16; Rules s 9
AU SDS note: Supplied with the product; seven content items mirroring PSTI.

Control: Conformity assessment route and third-party testing
Summary: Choose and run the assessment route each regime requires, from self-assessment to notified body, accredited lab or IPA evaluation body.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Route decision per product and regime; certificates and test reports.
Build to: CRA Class I/II via a notified body; otherwise US CTM (lab test for every product).
EU CRA clauses: Art 32; Annex VIII (Modules A, B, C, H)
EU CRA note: Notified body (Module B+C or H) for Class I unless a harmonised standard, common specification or substantial-level EU certification scheme is applied in full (Art 32(2)); Class II via B+C, H or an Art 27(9) scheme (Art 32(3)); FOSS may self-assess with public technical documentation (Art 32(5)).
UK PSTI clauses: SI 2023/1007 Sch 2; SI 2025/1267 (JC-STAR STAR-1 or CLS label)
US CTM clauses: FCC 24-26 (CyberLAB testing; CLA certification to ISO/IEC 17065)
US CTM note: Third-party test for every labelled product.
JC-STAR clauses: IPA (STAR-1/2 self-declaration; STAR-3/4 approved evaluation body)
JC-STAR note: Route rises with the level.
SG CLS note: Declaration at Levels 1-2; lab testing at Levels 3-4.

Summary: Keep declarations, statements and technical files for the longest period any regime requires.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Retention schedule tied to each placing on the market.
Build to: CRA and PSTI: 10 years or the support period, whichever is longer.
EU CRA note: 10 years or the support period, whichever is longer.
UK PSTI note: 10 years from issue or the defined support period, whichever is longer.
US CTM note: Retention period not read.
JC-STAR note: Validity, not retention.
SG CLS note: Not found in the specification read.

Control: Change control, substantial modification and label renewal
Summary: Assess each release for substantial modification and label impact; refresh declarations, registry entries and labels before expiry.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Release impact assessment per version; label expiry calendar.
Build to: CRA for modification; JC-STAR and CTM for fixed renewal cycles.
EU CRA note: A substantial modification may need a new conformity assessment and declaration.
UK PSTI note: Statement tied to product type and batch.
US CTM clauses: FCC 24-26 para 27 (update declaration on material change); renewal
US CTM note: Label-design, renewal and post-market proceeding opened late Oct 2026.
JC-STAR note: Labels expire unless extended.
AU SDS note: Statement tied to product type and batch.

Summary: Investigate suspected non-compliance, correct, withdraw or recall, inform authorities and users, and answer reasoned requests on time.
Evidence (one artefact, all regimes): Corrective-action procedure; regulator request log.
Build to: CRA and PSTI.
EU CRA note: Immediate correction, withdrawal or recall; information to MSAs on request.
UK PSTI note: Duties to investigate and act on compliance failures; compliance, stop and recall notices.
US CTM note: 20 days to cure; authorisation can be terminated.
JC-STAR note: Label can be withdrawn or revoked.
AU SDS note: Compliance, stop and recall notices; public notification.
